Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, full details below and attachments: 

- Primary processing: yes — we support region pinning so primary inference will be processed within the pinned geographic region (US, EU, or APAC) and will not be routed outside that region for inference. We can include contractual language in the DPA.
- Backups/replication: we do maintain asynchronous backups for HA and disaster recovery. By default snapshots are replicated to a designated secondary region (example: for US-primary, backup replicas are held in us-west-2 and us-east-1). We encrypt snapshots in transit and at rest. There are options to restrict replication to a single region (no cross-region replicas) for an additional operational SLA and cost.
- Subprocessors: attached CSV is our current list (as of 2026-02-20).
- DPA & evidence: attached Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf; SOC 2 link included in the follow-up.

If it's helpful, I can loop in Neha (Privacy) and Lauren (Legal) for the exact clause text. Are you available for a 30-minute call on Mon 02/23 or Tue 02/24?

Aditya / Lauren — quick notes and suggested DPA language below. High level: we can commit to region pinning for primary processing with clear carve-outs for operational failover. Backups are more sensitive — recommend offering two options in the commercial terms: default (encrypted cross-region replicas for DR) and an opt-in "Single-Region Backup" mode (additional operational constraints and a one-time configuration fee + ongoing monitoring SLA). Customer should acknowledge the tradeoffs (RTO/RPO).

Suggested DPA clause (draft):
"Redwood will ensure that primary processing of Customer Data for inference requests occurs within the geographic region(s) specified in Attachment A (\"Pinned Regions\"). Redwood will not route primary inference processing outside the specified Pinned Regions, except for (a) emergency operational failover where Redwood determines continued operation requires temporary cross-region processing, or (b) Customer-authorized cross-region transfers. In the event of emergency failover Redwood will notify Customer within 24 hours and provide a root-cause summary upon request."

Suggested paragraph on backups/replication:
"Redwood maintains encrypted snapshots of Customer Data for backup and disaster recovery. By default, snapshots may be replicated to one or more secondary regions to support availability and recovery objectives. Upon request, Customer may opt into a Single-Region Backup configuration that restricts backup replicas to the same region as primary processing, subject to (i) additional operational SLA terms, (ii) acceptance of a higher RTO/RPO, and (iii) an additional configuration fee as set forth in the Order Form."

Subprocessors: the CSV looks fine — we should confirm the monitoring supplier listed (TelemetryCo) is within the SOC2 scope; if not we need to elevate. I'll prepare a brief cover email and a redline to Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf with the suggested language.
